physical.notes: GTS3_SWDIAG on the cabinet port (internal column 0), read through dmd_u4_pb_r on VIA U4 PB3 without inversion. Every retained self-test run enters and steps the tests with it: two presses at 1 bring up TEST MODE and the menu, and each further press steps to the next self-test (runs lamp-matrix, solenoids, switch-matrix, front-door).

GTS3_SWTILT on the cabinet port, read through dmd_u4_pb_r on VIA U4 PB4 without inversion. Held at 1 inside the Switch Matrix Test it replaced the test screen with TILT (run switch-matrix), so the ROM reads it active at 1. GTS3.VBS names it swTilt = -7. The known-working script sets vpmNudge.TiltSwitch = 151 (line 255), which is not this address or any address System 3 publishes, so its nudge tilt pulses nothing the ROM reads: a defect in that table.

GTS3_SWSLAM on the cabinet port, read through VIA U4 CA1 on the DMD generation. A pulse at 1 inside the Front Door Test reset the game to attract mode (GAME OVER, run front-door), so the ROM reads it active at 1. GTS3.VBS names it swSlamTilt = -6.

physical.notes: GTS3_SWPRIN, which PinMAME reads back into the printer status that aux1_r returns for the optional communications adapter (printer) on the CPU board's auxiliary connector: at 1 the status reads ready, at 0 not connected. It is not a matrix switch, and held at 1 inside the Switch Matrix Test it put no SWITCH line of its own on the display (run switch-matrix). A recreation without the adapter leaves it at 0.

Strobe 0, return 0. In the Switch Matrix Test, holding public 0 at 1 alone displayed SWITCH:00 and the ROM's name "COIN CHUTE #1 -LEFT" (run switch-matrix). In play, the Front Door Test counted a coin on chute 1 for each pulse at 1 (run front-door), and two pulses gave one credit in attract mode (runs gameplay, tournament-door). Gladiators' game data sets no inverted-switch mask and gts3.c's xvia_0_a_r hands the CPU the complement of the matrix column, so public 1 is the closed contact the CPU sees, and the Switch Matrix Test reads ALL SWITCHES OPEN with every address at 0: the matrix contact rests open and closes when the device is actuated. inputs.label: Unused Flipper Column Lower Right End-of-Stroke (140)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (internal column 15, which core_updateSw uses for GEN_GTS3), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPEOSBIT = 0x01, published at 140 through gts3_m2sw(15, row) = 140 + row. locals.flipMask carries this end-of-stroke bit only when hw.flippers sets FLIP_EOS, and FLIP_SWNO(82,83) does not, so core_updateSw neither synthesizes it nor copies it anywhere: PinMAME models no end-of-stroke switch on this machine. A host write survives in the column, but the ROM cannot read it there: xvia_0_a_r reads the matrix only through core_getSwCol with the twelve-bit lamp/switch strobe, which reaches internal columns 1-12.

inputs.label: Lower Right Flipper Button (PinMAME Flipper Column)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (internal column 15, which core_updateSw uses for GEN_GTS3), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPBUTBIT = 0x02, published at 141 through gts3_m2sw(15, row) = 140 + row. This is the right cabinet flipper button as the ROM receives it. The driver declares FLIP_SWNO(82,83) with no FLIP_SOL, so with keyboard handling off (the LibPinMAME default) core_updateSw reads this bit as the host wrote it, copies it into matrix switch 83 on every update and fabricates the synthetic 45/46 flipper outputs from it while the game-over relay (32) is energized. mechanisms.behavior: The machine holds four balls (the power-up screen reads Install 4 Balls). A drained ball lands on the OUTHOLE switch (23); the OUTHOLE coil (29) kicks it into the trough, whose TROUGH switch (33) reports a ball, and the BALL RELEASE coil (28) feeds the lead ball into the shooter lane, where the SHOOTER LANE ROLLOVER (24) and the SHOOTER LANE (OPTO) (100) see it before the player plunges it. The PLUNGER GATE (13) is a post the known-working script drops while the output is on (lines 740-750). In the scripted game the ROM pulsed 13 at Start and served nothing from the trough, so the run does not show how the first ball reaches the shooter lane; when 23 rose it reset the 3-bank (10), energized 28 for about 0.7 s, fired 29 and energized the game-over relay (32) (run gameplay). The script models the trough as one four-ball stack with entry switch 23 and position switch 33 (lines 260-266).
mechanisms.label: Outhole, trough, ball release, shooter lane and plunger gate

mechanisms.behavior: The catapult is a moving rail ramp that must be shot with skill and timing to drop the ball into the Catapult Hole for 50,000,000 points (IPDB); the lamp matrix carries a CATAPULT 50M insert at the left hole (43) and a CATAPULT mode insert (73), and the Relay & Solenoid Test names a CATAPULT & BALL flasher (9). RAMP MOTOR RELAY (B) (23) switches the ramp's motor and RAMP MOTOR (30) senses its home. The known-working script runs the ramp as a one-solenoid reversing mechanism of 136 steps while 23 is on, with 30 closed at step 0 (lines 313-324), and swaps which ramp section is collidable as it moves (lines 531-540). The ROM energized 23 in its ball search and at the drain; opening and closing 30 did not make it release 23 (runs gameplay, mechanism-sensors), so the runs do not show the ROM's own stop condition.
mechanisms.label: Catapult moving rail ramp

mechanisms.behavior: Four ball holds: the TOP HOLE (switch 21, coil 7), the LEFT HOLE (switch 31, coil 6), the CENTER UPKICKER (switch 22, coil 11), which the script models as a vertical upkicker, and the RIGHT UPKICKER (switch 32, coil 12). Each switch held at 1 for 1.5 s during a game made the ROM fire its coil twice, and the ROM's ball search fires all four with the plunger gate (13) and the ramp motor relay (23) (runs gameplay, mechanism-sensors). The script models each as a saucer that holds its switch at 1 while the ball sits in it (lines 269-300).
mechanisms.label: Top hole, left hole, center and right upkickers

mechanisms.behavior: Three drop targets, DROP TARGET #1-#3 (15, 25, 35), reset together by 3 BANK RESET (10). The ROM fired the reset at power-up and when it served a ball after the drain; holding all three down for six seconds during the first ball drew no reset (run gameplay), so the run does not show when the ROM resets a completed bank in play. The script's dtBank writes the switches and raises the bank on 10 (lines 307-310 and 757-759).
mechanisms.label: 3-bank drop targets

mechanisms.behavior: Three pop bumpers (switches 10, 11 and 12, coils 1, 2 and 3) and two kicking targets (switches 13 and 14, coils 4 and 5), which the known-working script models as the two slingshots. System 3 has no special-solenoid circuit: the CPU reads each switch and fires its coil (pulses of 10, 11, 12 and 13 during a game fired 1, 2, 3 and 4; 5 was not observed, which PinMAME's four-frame solenoid smoothing could explain), so a consumer drives only the switch. The script assigns no callbacks to these coils and kicks with its own physics.
mechanisms.label: Pop bumpers and kicking targets

mechanisms.behavior: Four flippers (IPDB): a light press on a flipper button works only the lower flipper of that side, a heavy press the lower and the upper. The cabinet buttons fire them through the flipper circuit while the GAME OVER RELAY (Q, 32) is energized, so no CPU driver appears for them in the solenoid test; PinMAME fabricates 45-48 from the buttons at 141 and 143 while 32 is on. The ROM reads one switch per side, matrix switches 82 and 83 (named for the flipper sensor board), which core_updateSw copies from 143 and 141; neither the ROM nor PinMAME sees the heavy stage. The known-working script fires the upper flipper of each side together with the lower one (lines 870-886), so it does not model the two stages.
mechanisms.label: Four flippers on two two-stage buttons, cabinet-wired

mechanisms.behavior: The LIGHTBOX RELAY (A, 26) switches the backbox lightbox illumination and the TILT RELAY (T, 31) the playfield G.I., which goes out while it is energized (PinMAME's System 3 init types them as the A and T relays; the script turns its backbox and playfield G.I. off while each is on). The SHAKER MOTOR (25) shakes the cabinet (IPDB lists it), the KNOCKER (30) is in the cabinet, and TICKET/COIN METER (27) drives an optional ticket dispenser or coin meter.
mechanisms.label: Relays, shaker, knocker and coin meter
